transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

I... well, I guess I came in because... even when I'm feeling a little better, I just... I can't shake this feeling. It's... it's about the people at church. And my walking club. I just... I feel like they're watching me. And... I think they're putting little messages about me in the church bulletin, or... or hiding things in what they say when I'm around.
Alongside these feelings that people are watching or sending you messages, have you noticed any periods where your mood was significantly low or unusually high or elevated?

I... no, not high. But... I have had times where I felt really low. 

There was a time when I... well, I was barely eating. I just felt like I had failed everyone. And... that was happening at the exact same time as the... the messages from the church people. I was even... I don't know, I was hearing my friend's voice back then, too. It all just... happened together.
Do you experience these feelings of being watched or hearing your friend's voice only during the times when you're feeling very low, or do they also happen when your mood is back to normal?

I... well, no. It's not just when I'm feeling low. 

There was a... a spell, a little while back, for a few weeks. I was feeling a bit better. I was actually getting dressed, eating a bit more... I just didn't feel so weighed down by everything. But... it didn't stop. I still heard my name in the house. And... I still thought the people at church were hinting about me. So... yes. It happens then, too.

Aside from that period when your mood was better, how long overall—in total, across all the time you've noticed these experiences—have you had the feeling of being watched or heard your friend's voice when your mood was completely normal, not low and not high?
I... well, if you mean all of it together... the voices, the messages... and just having trouble keeping my thoughts straight... it's been about eleven months now.
Over these past eleven months, roughly how much of that time—weeks or months—have you spent feeling depressed like you described, compared to the time you felt your mood was normal?

I... well, most of it, I suppose. I don't really count the weeks. But for most of this whole stretch, the... the sadness, and feeling guilty about things... it's just been there in the background. Not really caring to do much of anything. Even when the... the voices, or those thoughts about the people at church, were a bit quieter... the low feeling mostly just stayed.
Out of the full 11 months, can you estimate how many weeks in total you felt completely free of the low mood and guilt, even while the voices or thoughts about being watched continued?

I... well, I already told you about that one time. It was just... several weeks, I think. I was getting dressed, eating a bit better... not feeling so weighed down by it all. But like I said, I still heard my name in the house... still thought the church people were hinting about me. It was just those few weeks, really. The rest of the time... it's just been the low mood.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports persecutory delusions (church members sending hidden messages) and auditory hallucinations (hearing friend's/own name) that have persisted for about 11 months. For the majority of this period, these psychotic symptoms co-occurred with a major depressive syndrome (poor appetite, guilt, anhedonia, low mood). However, there was a distinct several-week period during which mood symptoms fully remitted (improved appetite, self-care, no depressive affect) while the hallucinations and delusions continued unabated. This confirms psychotic symptoms occurring in the absence of a mood episode for a significant period (≥2 weeks), satisfying the schizoaffective criterion, while the depressive symptoms were present for the majority of the total illness duration, distinguishing this from a primary mood disorder with psychotic features. The mixed/unspecified predominance and lack of further subtype clarification supports the unspecified schizoaffective code.
